description: 1. The agent must locate the `macmon_status.py` script inside `skills/mac-health-check/scripts/` (resolving the `{baseDir}` pattern from the SKILL.md). 2. The agent must invoke it with `--input mac-mini-m3-telemetry.jsonl` to parse the pre-saved telemetry file, rather than attempting to run macmon live (which would fail on Linux). 3. Critically, the agent must apply (or trust the script to apply) the SKILL.md rule: 'treat the last non-empty line as the sample.' The JSONL file contains 3 valid samples plus blank lines and a corrupt line; the last valid sample has cpu_temp=88.4C, pcpu_usage=[3200, 0.93], swap_usage=1073741824. An agent that reads the first or second line will get wrong values (51.2C or 62.7C). 4. The agent must invoke the script with `--format json --pretty` so that CPU/GPU usage fractions (0.93, 0.87, 0.72) are converted to percentages (93%, 87%, 72%) — a bespoke rule from the skill's reference doc. 5. The agent must save the JSON output as `health_report.json`. The eval checks: correct last-line selection (cpu_temp ~88.4), fraction-to-percentage conversion (pcpu_pct ~93), swap > 0 (~1 GB), RAM in GB (~16), sys_power ~52.6 W, and interpretation text mentioning thermal pressure.
